cards: Justinian I was a Byzantine emperor of the sixth century CE.
Chlothar I was a Merovingian king of the Franks, the youngest son of Clovis I.
Gregory of Tours was a Gallo-Roman bishop of Tours from 573 and the author of the Histories, often called the History of the Franks.
Abraha was an Aksumite general who seized power in Himyar, in Yemen, in the 530s and ruled it, nominally as a vassal of Aksum, until about 570.
Pope Gregory I, known as Gregory the Great, was pope from 590 to 604.
Belisarius was the leading general of the Byzantine emperor Justinian I.
Kaleb was a king of Aksum who reigned c. 514–542 CE.
Kavad I was Sasanian King of Kings of Iran from 488 to 496 and again from 498 or 499 to 531.
Áedán mac Gabráin was king of Dál Riata, the Gaelic kingdom of Argyll and north-eastern Ireland, from about 574 to about 609.
Theodoric the Great was king of the Ostrogoths who invaded Italy at the request of Emperor Zeno, defeated Odoacer and ruled the peninsula from Ravenna from 493 to 526.
Alboin was king of the Lombards from about 560 and led them out of Pannonia into Italy in 568, soon after the Gothic Wars had exhausted the peninsula.
Khosrow I, also known as Anushirvan, was a Sasanian king who reigned in the sixth century CE and is remembered as one of the dynasty's greatest rulers.
r. 531–579 CE · Islamic Caliphates & Middle East
Mihirakula was a ruler of the Alchon Huns who controlled parts of north-western India in the early sixth century.
d. c. 540 CE · South & Southeast Asia
Maelgwn Gwynedd was king of Gwynedd in north-west Wales in the 6th century.
Simhavishnu was a king of the Pallava dynasty of Kanchipuram in southern India in the late 6th century.
Yasodharman was a ruler of Malwa in central India in the early 6th century, generally assigned to the Aulikara dynasty.
Yuwen Tai was a general of Xianbei descent who controlled the western half of the Northern Wei after it split in 534–535, ruling Western Wei as paramount general from Chang'an.
Boethius was a Roman senator and philosopher who served Theodoric the Great, becoming consul in 510 and master of offices.
Bridei son of Maelchon was a powerful king of the Picts in the second half of the 6th century.
Columbanus was an Irish monk from Bangor who travelled to Gaul around 590 and founded monasteries at Annegray, Luxeuil and Fontaine in the Frankish kingdom of Burgundy.
Liuvigild (Leovigild) was king of the Visigoths from about 568 to 586 and the main architect of their kingdom in Hispania.
Narses was an Armenian eunuch who rose to high office at the court of Justinian I and became one of his leading generals.
Phocas was a Byzantine emperor who seized power in 602 CE after a mutiny in which the emperor Maurice was murdered.
Authari was king of the Lombards from 584 to 590, chosen after a ten-year interregnum during which the dukes had ruled without a king.
Bahram Chobin was a Sasanian general of the Mihran family who defeated the Turks in 588–589.
Cosmas Indicopleustes, 'the India-voyager', was a sixth-century merchant from Alexandria who travelled the Red Sea and Indian Ocean trade routes and later became a monk.
Dugu Xin was a Xianbei general of the Western Wei dynasty and one of its Eight Pillars of State.
Emperor Wen of Sui, born Yang Jian, was a Northern Zhou official who seized power and founded the Sui dynasty in 581.
Emperor Wu of Chen, born Chen Baxian, was a Liang general who suppressed the rising of Lý Bí in northern Vietnam in 545 and helped defeat the rebel Hou Jing.
Gao Huan was a general of mixed Chinese and Xianbei culture who became the dominant figure in the Northern Wei during its collapse.
Garmul was a Berber king in western North Africa who attacked Byzantine Africa in the 570s, killing several imperial commanders, including the praetorian prefect Theodore.
Guntram was a Merovingian king of the Franks who ruled the kingdom of Burgundy from 561 to 592.
Hormizd IV was king of the Sasanian Empire from 579 to 590.
Hou Jing was a general of Eastern Wei who defected to the southern Liang dynasty after the death of Gao Huan in 547.
Saint Deiniol was a sixth-century Welsh churchman, traditionally regarded as the founder of the monastery of Bangor in Gwynedd and its first bishop.
Taspar Qaghan was ruler of the First Turkic Khaganate from 572 to 581, a son of the founder Bumin and successor of his brother Muqan.
Zhangsun Sheng was a Chinese general and diplomat of the Northern Zhou and Sui dynasties who specialised in relations with the Turks.
Childebert I was a Merovingian king of the Franks who ruled from Paris from 511 to 558.
Chlodomer was a Frankish king of the Merovingian dynasty, the second son of Clovis I and Clotilde.
Flavius Cresconius Corippus was a Latin poet from Roman North Africa in the 6th century.
